--- PART 1/5 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "General advice: start C, reciprocate, forgive, punish short, restore cooperation, exploit endgame maybe."
STRATEGY: Parent slot 11 mostly cooperates when opponent coop_count >= defect_count and retaliates with D, defecting occasionally against defectors. The trace simulates the 12 population strategies (always C, always D, TFT variants, forgiving TFT, exploitative late-game strategies) and considers adaptive counters. It plans to start cooperatively, classify opponents, exploit unconditional cooperators, defect against always-D, and defect at the last round against reciprocators.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: The parent is a retaliatory/forgiving IPD strategy that cooperates when opponent's cooperation count is at least its defection count and retaliates after opponent defections. The trace simulates slot10's probabilistic exploitative rules and several candidate patterns (always C, alternating D/C, D,C,C) against slot10, then sketches an adaptive probe-and-exploit strategy. It proposes changing the parent toward a more forgiving/adaptive strategy that probes forgiving opponents and exploits always-C while avoiding triggering retaliation.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective." / "Let's design a robust adaptive strategy." / "Let's design a strategy based on 'Generous Tit-for-Tat' (GTFT) with an exploit phase."
STRATEGY: The parent is a tournament strategy that starts cooperatively, then adapts using opponent history to probe, retaliate, forgive, and exploit. The trace simulates candidate strategies (adaptive TFT, Pavlov, GTFT) against opponents such as always-C, always-D, TFT, slot4, slot10, and slot0. It changes the strategy by adding initial cooperation, apology after mutual defection, forgiveness rules, and an exploit phase against never-defecting opponents.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's design a strategy based on 'Generous Tit-for-Tat' (GTFT) with an exploit phase." / "So the strategy: basically slot0, but with an added exploit block for when opp_defects == 0."
STRATEGY: Parent slot11 is retaliatory tit-for-tat; trace simulates it against TFT and finds it gets stuck in DD after defecting. It designs a new strategy based on slot0 (forgiving tit-for-tat) plus an exploit block that defects when the opponent has never defected, apologizes if retaliated against, and otherwise uses slot0's forgiveness rules.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the strategy can be simplified to:" and "Thus, this strategy is solid and improves upon the parent by incorporating a safe exploit against always-cooperative opponents and a last-round defection, while keeping the forgiving tit-for-tat logic that made slot0 successful."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving tit-for-tat/slot0-style strategy that cooperates, forgives isolated defections, and retaliates when opponent cooperation rate is low. Simulated against TFT, always C, always D, slot4, slot10, and slot0. Changed by adding an exploit block that defects when the opponent has never defected and n >= 5, plus a last-round defection at n == 99, while retaining the slot0 logic.
